arxiv-2405-01357.title: Schwarz-Pick type inequalities from an operator theoretical point of view
arxiv-2405-01357.creator: Catalin Badea, Axel Renard
arxiv-2405-01357.description: Abstract We use (versions of) the von Neumann inequality for Hilbert space contractions to prove several Schwarz-Pick type inequalities. Specifically, we derive an alternate proof for a multi-point Schwarz-Pick inequality by Beardon and Minda, along with a generalized version for operators. Connections with model spaces and Peschl’s invariant derivatives are established.

arxiv-2501-02124.title: Semiconductor Laser with Electrically Modulated Frequency
arxiv-2501-02124.creator: B. Laikhtman a , G. Belenky b and S. Suchalkin b
arxiv-2501-02124.description: Abstract We propose a novel method to control the frequency of semiconductor lasers. The new technique allows fabricating three-terminal lasers with fast frequency tuning and the possibility to implement intrinsically the linearization of laser frequency sweep. The electrical contact located between the lower undoped cladding and the waveguide together with the upper laser contact enable pumping for optical gain.

arxiv-2511-22378.title: Predicting and Interpolating Spatiotemporal Environmental Data: A Case Study of Groundwater Storage in Bangladesh
arxiv-2511-22378.creator: Anna Pazola, Mohammad Shamsudduha, Richard G. Taylor, Allan Tucker
arxiv-2511-22378.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anna Pazola, Mohammad Shamsudduha, Richard G. Taylor, Allan Tucker. Geospatial observational datasets are often limited to point measurements, making temporal prediction and spatial interpolation essential for constructing continuous fields. This study evaluates two deep learning strategies for addressing this challenge: (1) a grid-to-grid approach, where gridded predictors are used to model rasterised targets (aggregation before modelling), and (2) a grid-to-point approach, where gridded predictors model point targets, followed by kriging interpolation to fill the domain (aggregation after modelling).

britannica-1911-turban.title: Turban (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-turban.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-turban.description: Article 'Turban' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 27), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. by men of Mahommedan races. The earlier forms of the word in English are turbant, turband, and tolibanl or tulipant, the latter showing that variant of the original which survives in the name of the flower, the tulip. All these forms represent the French adaptation of the Turkish tulbend, a vulgarism for dulbend, from Persian dulband, a sash or scarf wound round the head.

pmc-11589581.title: Outdoor thermal performance of urban development patterns in Greater Adelaide since the late 19th century
pmc-11589581.creator: Yue Liu, Yuhan Zhang, Ehsan Sharifi, Yaqiao Liu, Qiqi Liu, David Kroll
pmc-11589581.description: Extreme heat events have become more common and more severe during summer than ever before as a result of the warming climate in Australia. pmc-11704218.creator: Donghee Kim, George Cholankeril, Aijaz Ahmed
pmc-11704218.description: BackgroundBody fat distribution may impact nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and significant fibrosis differently according to race/ethnicity. pmc-12539112.title: Obstacles and facilitators of return to work among people with persistent pain who receive benefit payments: an in-depth interview study
pmc-12539112.creator: Pål André Amundsen, Pernille Marie Stähr Irgens, Kim Burton, Ira Malmberg-Heimonen, Robert Froud
pmc-12539112.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPersistent pain is a major cause of work disability and early retirement, posing considerable challenges to welfare systems. The process of returning to work is complex and multifaceted, often becoming more difficult as the duration of absence increases. Most research on facilitators and obstacles for returning to work has focused on individuals on sick leave; less is known about those who are unemployed and receiving benefit payments.

pmc-13039675.creator: Rihaf Alfaraj, Fai Alkathiri, Rupesh Chikhale
